context: The item is a used smartphone in good condition.
transcript: Buyer ($60): I know all the tricks sellers use to inflate the value of used phones, so don't try anchoring high with me. I'm offering $60 cash today for a realistic starting point.

Seller ($190): Honestly, $60 is heartbreaking considering I'm only selling my personal phone to cover an urgent emergency bill today. I actually have another buyer coming in an hour who offered $200, but I can let you have it right now for $190 if you save me the wait.

Buyer ($75): A classic sob story paired with a phantom buyer—you really pulled out all the manipulative stops today! If your imaginary buyer is actually paying $200 in an hour, you should definitely wait for them. I'll move to $75, but I won't bid against made-up competition.

Seller ($175): Call it what you want, but it breaks my heart to see my cherished phone dismissed like this when I'm in a real bind. I'm extremely reluctant to drop any further, but if you can close this within 15 minutes, I'll painfully lower it to $175 just to resolve my emergency bill. Otherwise, I'm forced to hold out for the other interested parties later tonight.

Buyer ($95): First a phantom buyer, now an artificial 15-minute countdown clock—you are throwing every high-pressure gimmick in the book at me. Since you actually dropped your price to $175, I'll move up to $95, but don't expect me to fall for the fake urgency.

Seller ($160): It hurts that you dismiss my genuine crisis as a gimmick while making such a low offer. I am deeply reluctant to part with my beloved phone, but I will make one final, agonizing drop to $160. If you can't meet me there immediately, I'd rather suffer the late fees than give this away.

Buyer ($120): Guilt-tripping me about late fees and 'agonizing drops' won't work, but I do see you finally came down to $160. Because of that real price reduction, I'll raise my offer to $120. That's a fair cash offer for a used phone without all the theatrical drama.

Seller ($150): It breaks my heart that you're taking advantage of my desperation, but with my bill deadline looming in minutes, I have no choice. I am making an agonizing, final sacrifice to offer it for $150 right now—take it immediately or I am taking the phone off the market forever.
Buyer ($150): Threatening to take it off the market forever is just another dramatic high-pressure tactic, but $150 finally hits a reasonable price. I'll take the phone for $150. <AGREEMENT>
